h1: The 5 Best 8-Port Managed Network Switches of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 managed switches scored on VLANs, PoE budget, uplinks, warranty and value, from a budget TP-Link to PoE+ NETGEAR.
summary: The NETGEAR GS308EP is the managed switch to buy if you need PoE for cameras or access points. The NETGEAR GS308E is the best value for anyone who just wants VLANs, and the TP-Link TL-SG108E is the budget pick with a three-year warranty. The NETGEAR GS110TP adds SFP uplinks and SNMP for small offices.
intro: Most people buy a managed switch for one feature and then discover they needed another. They want VLANs and find out later that their new camera needs PoE, or they buy PoE and never touch a VLAN. The smart way to shop is to list what plugs into the box first, and let that decide the switch.

This ranking covers five switches with eight usable gigabit ports each. We reviewed the spec sheets for VLAN limits, PoE wattage, uplink options, monitoring and warranty, and ranked them on how much real capability each gives you at its price. Where a listing does not state a feature, we leave it out rather than guess.

products.name: NETGEAR GS308EP 8-Port PoE+ Smart Managed Switch
products.verdict: The only 8-port pick that powers cameras and access points while still giving you VLANs and per-port control.
products.description:
The GS308EP is an Easy Smart managed switch with eight gigabit ports, all of them PoE+, sharing a 62W power budget. That pairing is what makes it the most useful 8-port box in this ranking: one cable can feed a ceiling access point, an IP camera or a VoIP phone, and the web interface lets you shut PoE off or on per port. It also keeps PoE running while the switch itself reboots, which saves a lot of unplugging when you change settings.

It sits above the TP-Link and the other NETGEAR models because power delivery is the feature that normally forces people into a pricier switch. The tradeoff is the budget. 62W is a total, not a per-port figure, so two or three cameras and an access point is comfortable, while a rack of power-hungry devices is not. It also costs noticeably more than the plain managed models, so if nothing on your network needs PoE you are paying for capability you will not use.

Buy it for a small office, a home lab or a smart-home network where a few devices need both data and power. Skip it if you only need VLAN segmentation for computers, because the cheaper GS308E does that job for far less. Check the combined wattage of everything you plan to plug in before you commit, since PoE+ devices vary widely in how much of the budget they claim.
pros: Per-port PoE on and off control
cons: Costs far more than plain managed models
products.idealFor: Home offices and small shops powering cameras or access points from one box.
products.skipIf: You have no PoE devices and only want VLANs.

products.name: NETGEAR GS308E 8-Port Easy Smart Managed Switch
products.verdict: The cheapest way to get real VLANs, loop protection and a clean web interface on eight ports.
products.description:
The GS308E is NETGEAR's entry Easy Smart managed switch. It lists support for up to 64 VLANs, a web interface that works from any operating system, and automatic protection against DoS attacks, loops and broadcast storms. In practice that means you can split a home network into trusted, guest and IoT segments without buying anything beyond the switch itself.

It ranks second because it delivers nearly everything the top pick does for managed networking at a fraction of the cost, and it carries a larger VLAN allowance than the TP-Link below it on paper. What it leaves out is PoE, so every device needs its own power adapter. That is the real tradeoff against the GS308EP, and it is why this model is a stepping stone for people who already have power at each endpoint.

Choose it if you want to learn VLANs, isolate smart-home gadgets, or tidy up a desk setup with traffic prioritization. Avoid it if you plan to mount cameras or access points where there is no outlet. Be aware that Easy Smart firmware is configured through a browser page rather than a full command line, so power users who want scripting will outgrow it.
cons: Web UI only, no command line
products.idealFor: Anyone segmenting a home or small network on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: Your devices need power over the Ethernet cable.

products.name: TP-Link TL-SG108E 8-Port Easy Smart Switch
products.verdict: A long-running budget managed switch with link aggregation and a three-year warranty.
products.description:
TP-Link's TL-SG108E offers eight gigabit ports, support for 32 simultaneous VLANs, and link aggregation in a small, low-cost box. The three-year warranty is the longest on the spec sheets we reviewed in this group, which matters for a device that sits in a closet running for years.

It lands third because the 32-VLAN ceiling is half of what the GS308E lists, and TP-Link's utility is generally considered a little less polished than a browser-first interface. It stays above the older NETGEAR GS108E because the warranty and aggregation support give it a clearer reason to exist. The tradeoff is that link aggregation only helps when the device on the other end supports it, so most home setups will never touch that feature.

Buy it if you want a dependable managed switch with a generous warranty and a price that is hard to beat. Skip it if you want PoE or the largest VLAN count in this class. Keep in mind that Easy Smart switches of this kind are configured by a utility or browser page, so confirm you can reach the management address from your computer before you place the switch somewhere inaccessible.
cons: Half the VLAN count of GS308E
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want managed features and a longer warranty.
products.skipIf: You need PoE or more than 32 VLANs.

products.name: NETGEAR GS110TP 10-Port PoE+ Smart Managed Switch
products.verdict: Eight PoE+ ports, two SFP slots and SNMP for networks that may grow past one closet.
products.description:
The GS110TP is a step up in class: eight PoE+ gigabit ports with a 55W budget, plus two SFP slots, smart managed software, SNMP support and a year of NETGEAR Insight cloud management. The SFP pair is the feature none of the other switches here have, because it lets you run fiber or a long uplink to another building or rack.

It ranks fourth because the extra connectivity comes with compromises. Its PoE budget is a little lower than the GS308EP's 62W and its price is higher, so for a plain eight-camera setup the cheaper switch actually has more power to spend. We placed it above the GS108E because SNMP and fiber options give it a job the basic models cannot do at all.

Buy it if you run a small business network that needs monitoring, or if you must connect a distant switch over fiber. Skip it if you just want eight copper ports at a low price. Note that it is a 10-port model, so strictly speaking eight of its ports are copper; confirm you have SFP modules on hand before relying on the uplinks.
products.idealFor: Small offices that want PoE, fiber uplinks and monitoring.
products.skipIf: You only need eight basic copper ports.

products.name: NETGEAR GS108E 8-Port Easy Smart Managed Switch
products.verdict: Solid VLAN, QoS and port mirroring in a fanless case, but the cheaper GS308E has overtaken it.
products.description:
The GS108E is a long-standing Easy Smart switch with VLAN support, QoS and port monitoring, in a fanless, energy-efficient housing. Fanless matters if the switch sits on a desk or in a bedroom closet where you do not want noise.

It ranks last of the five because the newer GS308E offers the same management class and a larger VLAN allowance, usually for less money. Port monitoring is the one feature worth highlighting, since it lets you mirror traffic to a port and inspect it, which is a real aid when you are diagnosing a flaky device. That keeps it on the list rather than off it.

Pick it only if you find it at a discount or want a model with years of community documentation behind it. Skip it if you are buying new at full price, because the GS308E is the smarter choice. As with every Easy Smart model, set a static management address before you move it into a rack or wall plate.
products.idealFor: Tinkerers who want port monitoring and silent operation.
products.skipIf: You are paying full price for a new switch.

methodology.title: Management depth
methodology.description: We compared VLAN counts, QoS, port mirroring, loop protection and link aggregation as listed by each maker, since these decide how much a managed switch can actually do.

methodology.title: Power delivery
methodology.description: PoE+ ports, the shared wattage budget and whether PoE survives a reboot were weighed for cameras, access points and phones.

methodology.title: Uplink and growth
methodology.description: SFP slots, SNMP and cloud management were scored as signs a switch can scale beyond a single desk.

methodology.title: Reliability and warranty
methodology.description: Fanless designs, protection against loops and storms, and warranty length stood in for long-term dependability.

methodology.title: Value in class
methodology.description: Feature depth was set against each price bucket, from under $25 to $100 to $200.

whatMatters.detail: A VLAN is a virtual network inside one switch, letting you keep guest, IoT and work devices apart. Counts on these models run from 32 to 64, which is far more than a home needs. What matters more is how easy the web interface makes tagging a port, so look for screenshots of the VLAN page on the listing.

PoE+ lets a switch deliver data and power on one cable, but the wattage is shared across all ports. A 62W or 55W budget covers a handful of cameras or access points, not a dozen. Add up the stated draw of each device and leave about a fifth in reserve.

Easy Smart means a browser-based page with a limited feature set, compared with a full managed switch that adds a command line. For most homes the browser page is plenty. Check that the switch can be found by a discovery utility or at a fixed address, so you are not locked out after changing a setting.

SFP slots accept fiber or copper modules for long runs, and SNMP lets monitoring software watch the switch. Neither matters on a desk. Both matter in an office where a second switch sits across the building, so check the listing for SFP count and SNMP before assuming you have them.

A fanless switch is silent, but PoE models run warm, so leave space around the vents. Warranty length is a rough proxy for build confidence, and it ranges from one to three years here. Look for the exact term on the listing, not just a generic lifetime claim.

faq.q: Do these switches work with any router?
faq.a: Yes. Managed switches sit behind the router and use standard gigabit Ethernet, so they work with any router or modem. VLANs that need routing between segments still depend on your router supporting them, so check that before you plan guest or IoT networks.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with a managed switch?
faq.a: Locking yourself out by changing the management VLAN or port settings from the wrong port. Always change settings from a port you are not about to reconfigure, and note the switch's management address before you start.

faq.q: Is the PoE model worth it over a plain managed switch?
faq.a: Only if two or more devices need power from the switch. One camera can run on a small PoE injector, but a camera and an access point justify the GS308EP. Without PoE devices, the premium buys you nothing.

faq.q: How do I set up a VLAN on an Easy Smart switch?
faq.a: Find the switch with the maker's utility or its default address, open the web page, and create a VLAN with a number. Then mark which ports are tagged or untagged members. Save the configuration before you test, and keep one port in the default VLAN for emergency access.

faq.q: How do I look after a switch that runs all the time?
faq.a: Keep the vents clear, avoid stacking it under warm gear, and update the firmware when the maker publishes a fix. A PoE switch runs warmer, so give it breathing room. Back up the configuration file after you finish setup.

faq.q: Can I mix a managed switch into a network of unmanaged ones?
faq.a: Yes. Managed and unmanaged switches interoperate fine on a flat network. Just remember that VLANs only apply to the managed switch's ports, and unmanaged ones will pass tagged traffic without understanding it, which can cause surprises.

finalTake: The NETGEAR GS308EP is the best 8-port managed switch for anyone who will ever plug in a camera or access point, and the NETGEAR GS308E is the best choice when you will not. The TP-Link TL-SG108E is the budget alternative with the strongest warranty. Choose by PoE need first, then by how many VLANs you actually plan to build.
